description:

For game implementation details see:

name: open_spiel_connect_four

action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.status: OK; Setup step; model not called.

info.agentSelfReportedStatus: OK; Setup step; model not called.

This is an early-game position where no immediate threats, wins, or blocks exist for either player. action.thoughts:
The current board has X pieces at the bottom of columns 2 and 3, with my O stacked directly above the X in column 3. This leaves an open threat: on X's next turn, X can drop in column 4 (or symmetrically column 1) to create three X's in a row along the bottom. That would create a double threat (fork) on both open ends of the line (columns 0/1 and 5/6), which I could block in only one place, allowing X to win on the following turn.

I must therefore respond in a way that occupies one of the critical extension points (column 1 or 4) to ensure that any three-in-a-row X can only threaten a single remaining spot. Column 4 is the superior choice of the two because:
- It is more central and closer to my existing O.
- It directly connects diagonally with my O at row 4, column 3 (forming a two-piece diagonal).
- It blocks the right-side extension while leaving only a single-threat response (column 0) if X instead extends leftward.

No other column prevents the fork. Moves such as column 2 (creating a horizontal pair with my O) or column 3 (stacking vertically) allow X to immediately play column 4 and force the win. Column 4 is therefore the only optimal move that both defends and improves my position.

All other positions are empty, making this an early-game position with no immediate wins possible for either player (no player has 3 in a row, and one move cannot create 4 in a row).

O's pieces at (row 4, col 3) and (row 5, col 5) are currently disconnected. Placing O in column 4 drops the piece to the lowest available spot at (row 4, col 4). This single move connects all three of O's pieces:
- Horizontally at row 4: O at cols 3-4.
- Diagonally: O at (row 4, col 4) and (row 5, col 5).

This creates multiple extension paths for O (e.g., future horizontal at row 4 cols 2/5/6, vertical in col 4, or the diagonal continuing to row 3 col 3). It also places O directly above X's piece in col 4, limiting X's vertical options there.

Alternative moves are inferior:
- Column 2 or 6 places O at row 5 but leaves O's pieces disconnected and isolated from the existing (row 4, col 3).
- Column 3 stacks vertically in col 3 but does not connect to the (row 5, col 5) piece.
- Column 5 creates a short vertical in col 5 but leaves a gap at row 4 col 4 and does not connect horizontally to (row 4, col 3).
- Edge columns (0 or 1) are too far from existing pieces to build threats efficiently.

X has an adjacent pair at row 5 cols 3-4 and could potentially create a 3-in-a-row threat by playing in col 2 on the next turn. However, O can respond by blocking at col 1 without issue, and O's stronger central connections from the col 4 move outweigh this (O will have initiative for counter-threats like building a 3-in-a-row at row 4 cols 3-5). Column 4 is the optimal balance of connectivity, central control, and long-term forcing potential in this configuration.
